_comment: Strategy layer for offline.carino.systems. Source of truth is /home/carino/Github/OFFLINE.md sections 1, 9, 10 and 11; when that document changes, change this file in the same commit. Extend by appending objects, never by renaming an existing id (ids are kebab-case, unique across the whole file, and are used as anchors; phases[].id is the one exception — it is the 0-6 integer, and it is a key in the carino.offline.phases localStorage array, so renaming it would silently untick every existing reader's playbook). threats[].likelihood is one of high|medium|low; threats[].layer holds a layers[].id (lowercase l0-l5; the display form lives in layers[].label). breaks[].severity is one of hard (no offline answer exists), soft (degrades, recovers on reconnect) or avoidable (a purchasing or migration decision removes it). Keep breaks[].why honest: an entry that admits there is no mitigation is worth more than one that invents one. Omit any field you are not sure of rather than filling it.

principles.t: Everything works with the WAN cable pulled
principles.d: Internet is an optimization, not a requirement. Anything that only works while the link is up is a feature, not infrastructure, and gets budgeted as one.

principles.t: The same URL works online and offline
principles.d: Split-horizon DNS answers retina.carino.systems with a LAN address inside the building and a public one outside. Nobody learns two address books, and printed QR codes, bookmarks and NFC tags never need reprinting.

principles.t: Lower layers never depend on higher ones
principles.d: L2 (the intranet) must not depend on L3 (the overlay) or above. If WireGuard, the VPS and the whole outward path die, the intranet does not notice. The dependency arrow only ever points down.

This plan handles infrastructure denial: blocked resolvers, a seized domain, filtered transit, a dead link. It does not handle a targeted adversary with physical access or legal compulsion. Those are not engineering problems and pretending otherwise produces bad engineering.
If a device needs a vendor account to function, it does not enter the building. Checked at purchase time, because firmware rollback after the fact almost never works.

principles.t: Physical media is a layer, not a fallback
principles.d: Sneakernet moves at 60 km/h with effectively infinite bandwidth and zero DPI. It is the only layer that survives everything, so it gets a production line and a registry, not a drawer of unlabelled discs.

layers.label: L0 Power
layers.d: Two UPS units with NUT for graceful shutdown, plus a 1 kWh LiFePO4 station carrying the core rack. Solar is optional and only appears in Tier C.
layers.rule: The shutdown order is written on paper and has been tested. A pool corrupted on the way down costs more than the outage that caused it.

layers.label: L1 Compute
layers.d: Proxmox VE 9 on ZFS: node A primary, node B a replica in a second building receiving zfs send nightly. LXC for light services, KVM for the rest.
layers.rule: Anything that exists only on node A is not backed up, whatever the snapshot schedule says.

layers.label: L2 Intranet
layers.d: MikroTik core, seven VLANs, own recursive and authoritative DNS (Technitium + Unbound), own CA (step-ca, 10-year root), own GPS-disciplined clock. This is the product; everything else is scaffolding around it.
layers.rule: L2 never depends on L3 or above. VLAN 40 (printers, 3D printers, IoT) and VLAN 99 (PACS) have no default gateway at all.

layers.label: L3 Overlay
layers.d: WireGuard to an offshore VPS, Yggdrasil for DNS-independent addressing, and obfuscated transports staged in escalation order. Exists to sync mirrors and keep the public face alive under filtering.
layers.rule: Only for reaching out. Nothing internal may depend on it, and if it does that is a bug to file, not a configuration to document.

layers.label: L4 Radio
layers.d: Meshtastic on 915 MHz, roughly $48 a node, 2-15 km line of sight, no infrastructure of any kind. Ham and Winlink stay optional pending the IFT licence question.
layers.rule: Text only. LoRa throughput is measured in bytes per second, so design the message formats for that and not for convenience.

layers.label: L5 Sneakernet
layers.d: M-DISC and BD-R optical, USB, printed manuals and IP cards, NFC tags, 3D-printed spare parts and enclosures. Slow, unblockable, and the layer most plans skip.
layers.rule: Every disc carries a README, SHA256SUMS and 10% PAR2, and is read-back verified before it leaves the building. A disc that was never verified is not a backup.

threats.failure: Public DNS resolvers block or NXDOMAIN the zone
threats.works: Own recursive resolver plus an authoritative internal zone, so resolution never leaves the building
threats.useless: A VPN on its own, which still has to resolve a name somewhere
threats.note: This is the cheapest attack to run and therefore the one to assume first.

threats.failure: ISP deep packet inspection blocks the domain or the TLS SNI
threats.works: Internal names, IP-literal fallback with certs that carry IP SANs, and the overlay for anything genuinely outbound
threats.useless: Switching to another DNS provider, which changes who answers but not who is in the path

threats.failure: Domain suspended or seized by the registrar or ccTLD operator
threats.works: carino.internal names, an internal CA, and printed cards carrying IP literals and Yggdrasil addresses
threats.useless: Any countermeasure that still starts with a DNS lookup of the seized name
threats.note: .internal is ICANN-reserved for private use since 2024, so it will never collide with a real TLD.

threats.failure: Let's Encrypt becomes unreachable and public certs expire on schedule
threats.works: step-ca with a real ACME endpoint and a 10-year root; Caddy renews internally forever with no internet
threats.useless: Buying a long-lived public certificate, since the maximum lifetime drops to 47 days by 2029
threats.note: Follows any of the blocking scenarios above rather than occurring on its own.

threats.failure: Clocks drift after weeks offline and quietly break TLS, TOTP and DICOM timestamps
threats.works: A GPS/PPS hat on a Pi feeding chrony, roughly $90 for the whole kit, serving time to the whole intranet
threats.useless: Reaching for public NTP pools that are on the far side of the same cut
threats.note: The most underrated line in the whole build. Failures surface two to three weeks in, look unrelated to each other, and cost a day to diagnose.

threats.works: LAN-local everything, plus sneakernet for anything bulky
threats.useless: Paying for a faster WAN, which buys more of a pipe that is being inspected anyway

threats.failure: Full internet cut, regional or national
threats.works: Local mirrors, media, games and knowledge base already on disk, with LoRa for text between sites
threats.useless: Cloud backup, which is exactly as reachable as the thing that just disappeared
threats.note: Low probability, non-zero, and the only scenario the entire content layer exists for.

threats.works: UPS plus a LiFePO4 station on the core rack, with NUT triggering a tested shutdown order
threats.useless: A bigger server, which just drains the battery faster
threats.note: Medium is the honest number for Mexico, not a hedge.

threats.failure: Hardware fails while the link is down
threats.works: Spare parts on the shelf, ZFS redundancy, and a replica at the second site
threats.useless: A warranty, since an RMA needs shipping and a working internet to open the ticket

threats.failure: A cloud SaaS provider locks the account out
threats.works: Self-hosted equivalents already running in production, with the data already in them
threats.useless: Planning to export the data later; the export path is the first thing a lockout removes

threats.failure: A vendor disables a device remotely or ends its cloud service
threats.works: Hardware chosen at purchase time for LAN-only operation, parked on VLAN 40 with no WAN route
threats.useless: Rolling firmware back after the fact, which is usually blocked and always late
threats.note: Printers and 3D printers are the usual casualties. This is why Prusa over Bambu: Bambu's LAN mode is a vendor policy, not a property of the device.

threats.failure: Targeted adversary with physical access to the building
threats.works: Nothing here. Encryption at rest buys minutes and an accurate inventory of what was taken
threats.useless: More network security, which is defending a door that is no longer the way in
threats.note: Explicitly out of scope. Stating it plainly is more useful than a countermeasure that would not survive contact.

threats.failure: Legal compulsion to hand over keys, data or the domain
threats.works: Nothing here either. This plan is about infrastructure denial, not coercion
threats.useless: Any technical measure, since the compulsion applies to the operator rather than the system
threats.note: The second of the two failure modes this plan refuses to design around.

phases.name: Escape kit
phases.deliverable: Zone file backups, git bundles of every fleet repo, registrar lock, a crown-jewel M-DISC set and a printed emergency runbook
phases.exit: If the domain vanished tonight, I would lose nothing permanent
tasks: git bundle create one file per fleet repo, around twenty of them; a bundle is a single file, self-contained, and clonable with no server
Export the DNS zone file and the DNSSEC keys and store them alongside the bundles
Enable registrar lock and write down the move-the-zone-in-under-an-hour procedure while nobody is in a hurry
Export Vaultwarden, print the TOTP seeds, put the sheet in the fire safe
Burn the crown jewels to two or three M-DISC BD-R with SHA256SUMS and 10% PAR2, then verify the read-back
Print the emergency runbook: cold boot of node A, restore from cold HDD, root CA recovery, UPS shutdown order, backup codes
Buy the cold-spare Blu-ray burner now; drives are being discontinued industry-wide and the media outlives them

phases.name: Core
phases.deliverable: Node A, MikroTik core, VLANs, Technitium, step-ca, Caddy, GPS-NTP and the Homepage hub
phases.exit: Every fleet tool reachable at all three name tiers with a valid cert, WAN unplugged
tasks: Build node A on Proxmox VE 9: mirrored NVMe for VM storage, six 16 TB drives in RAIDZ2 for bulk
Bring up the RB5009 core with the seven VLANs; 40 and 99 get no gateway at all, not merely a deny rule
Technitium authoritative for both carino.systems (split-horizon) and carino.internal, Unbound behind it as the recursor
step-ca with a 10-year root, Caddy's ACME client pointed at it, one config block per service
Issue every internal cert with its IP SAN as well as its names, so https://10.20.0.30 still works when DNS is dead
GPS/PPS hat on a Pi feeding chrony, serving time to the whole intranet
Homepage at http://hub/, laid out search-first like the public hub so muscle memory transfers
Publish the root CA fingerprint on the printed IP card before anyone has a reason to need it

phases.name: Fleet Offline Edition
phases.deliverable: carino-offline.iso, the USB folder build, a docker compose bundle, service workers and a signed release
phases.exit: A fresh laptop with no internet boots the USB and uses every tool
tasks: Audit every repo for a stray absolute URL or external fetch; the fonts convention says this is already clean, so verify it rather than assume it
Add a service worker per tool for install-to-homescreen and real PWA offline behaviour
Write a Makefile that clones every fleet repo at a pinned commit and emits a Ventoy-compatible ISO
Ship tools.json with LAN-relative URLs so the hub's search routing behaves identically offline
Verify the Carino Bridge handoff over file:// and over http://hub.carino.internal; Media to Metadata and PACS to DICOM-editor are the flows that matter
Include the es, pt-BR, ja and ru locale sets; offline should not mean English-only
Sign the ISO and publish the SHA-256 in the git tag and on the printed card

phases.name: Content
phases.deliverable: Kiwix, the media stack, LANCache, selective distro mirrors and permanent game servers
phases.exit: A month offline is comfortable, not merely survivable
tasks: Kiwix: Wikipedia ES and EN with images at roughly 180 GB, plus Wikimed, Wikivoyage and the Stack Exchange dump at about 100 GB
Media stack: Jellyfin, Navidrome, Audiobookshelf, Komga, Calibre-Web, Immich, Paperless-ngx, and Nextcloud with CalDAV/CardDAV so the phones stop needing Google
LANCache first, before the mirrors; it is the highest-value single container here and it makes a throttled WAN a non-issue for bulk downloads
Selective distro mirrors only: Fedora current and n-1 at about 600 GB, Debian and Ubuntu LTS at about 800 GB. Mirror the arch and releases actually in use
Pull-through caches rather than full mirrors for PyPI (devpi), npm (Verdaccio) and container images (registry:2)
Permanent servers for the libre LAN titles: 0 A.D., OpenTTD, Xonotic, Veloren, Mindustry, Wesnoth, plus headless Minecraft and Factorio
Point ArchiveBox at the bookmark bar and run it monthly; it grows past 200 GB and that is fine
If the GPU lands early: Ollama with a ~30B open-weight model and a RAG index over Kiwix, Paperless and the fleet docs

phases.name: Sneakernet line
phases.deliverable: The disc pipeline, the print artifacts, the NFC rollout and a mirrored 3D model library
phases.exit: 20 discs and 50 NFC tags produced end to end without touching the internet
tasks: Stand up the disc pipeline as one script: burn, PAR2 at 10%, read-back verify, sha256sum -c, label, register
UDF 2.60 for Blu-ray, ISO9660 plus Joliet and Rock Ridge for DVD and CD; README.txt and SHA256SUMS at the root of every disc without exception
Log every disc in Paperless: contents, date, hash, and who holds a copy
Print and laminate the IP card and hand one to every household and staff member; this is the break-glass artifact
Quick-start cards per fleet tool and saddle-stitched manuals for the appliance and for PACS
Encode the NFC set: NTAG215 tap-to-open stickers, a Wi-Fi join card at reception, NTAG215 asset tags linked to Topo records
Give every NFC tag a printed QR twin on the same surface; not every phone has usable NFC and every phone has a camera
Mirror the 3D model library into Forgejo with its licence files, the sliced gcode and the printer profile. A model that cannot be printed during an outage is not a model you have

phases.name: Second site and radio
phases.deliverable: Node B replication, cold HDD rotation, the Meshtastic mesh, and the offshore VPS with obfuscated transports staged
phases.exit: Node A destroyed, serving from site B in under 24 hours
tasks: Decide the second site: different building, ideally a different power feed and neighbourhood. Everything in this phase blocks on that one choice
Node B online and receiving zfs send nightly
Cold rotation on two 20 TB LUKS externals, swapped monthly, one always off-premises
Four Meshtastic nodes in printed enclosures, with the antennas actually mounted high rather than left on a desk
Offshore VPS with WireGuard as the primary outbound path
Configure shadowsocks-2022, Xray-VLESS-REALITY, Hysteria2 and obfs4 bridges now, while they are still trivially downloadable
Yggdrasil on every node, with the addresses printed on the IP card; this is the domain-seized continuity path

phases.name: Drills
phases.deliverable: A quarterly blackout drill with the WAN physically unplugged, and a ticket list from each one
phases.exit: Every failure found becomes a ticket; the drill is over only when the list is empty
tasks: Quarterly 72-hour blackout drill, cable out at the router
Quarterly restore test from cold media, performed against the printed runbook alone
Annual disc integrity verify across the archive: sha256sum -c plus PAR2
Reprint and redistribute the IP card on any renumbering
Update OFFLINE.md after every phase completion and every drill; it is a living document or it is fiction

breaks.why: Stamping a CFDI requires reaching the SAT or a PAC. There is no offline mode, and an unstamped document is not an invoice in any sense that matters legally or to a client's accountant.
breaks.mitigation: Keep the LTE line alive specifically for this. During an outage, issue a paper record and stamp it when the link returns; the catch-up is bookkeeping, not exposure.

breaks.why: SPEI clears through Banxico. There is nothing to self-host, nothing to mirror, and no degraded mode. Money simply does not move.
breaks.mitigation: None. Hold enough cash to cover about a week of operations and accept the exposure rather than pretending a workaround exists.

breaks.thing: SMS and voice 2FA to third parties
breaks.why: The second factor lives on someone else's network. If the carrier is down, or the service only offers SMS, the account is unreachable no matter how well the building is running.
breaks.mitigation: Move every account that supports TOTP to TOTP, with seeds in Vaultwarden and printed in the safe. Audit the SMS-only remainder once a year and close what can be closed; the rest is a known liability, not a solved problem.

breaks.why: Activation phones home on its own schedule, and a workstation that deactivates in week three of an outage is a self-inflicted wound with no local fix.
breaks.mitigation: Run Linux wherever it is a choice. Keep two or three pre-activated VMs snapshotted for the software that genuinely needs Windows, and treat the snapshot as the licence.

breaks.why: A periodic licence check is a WAN dependency wearing a costume. The software stops when the link stops, and the vendor considers that working as intended.
breaks.mitigation: FreeCAD, Blender, Krita, Inkscape, PrusaSlicer. Where a perpetual licence still exists, buy it and archive the installer next to the key.

breaks.why: Steam offline mode only works if you logged in recently and pre-downloaded, and streaming licences are not downloads at all. Every DRM check is a WAN dependency that was paid for.
breaks.mitigation: Buy GOG by default; DRM-free installers archive as ordinary files. Pair Steam with LANCache and treat it as best-effort, never as foundation.

breaks.why: Firmware lives on a vendor's site and vanishes without notice, outage or not. The failure surfaces years later, when a board needs reflashing and the download page is a 404.
breaks.mitigation: Archive firmware per device model at purchase time, on the SMB share, next to the manual and the driver.

breaks.thing: Public CA certificates for the WAN-facing site
breaks.why: If Let's Encrypt is unreachable the public certificate expires on a schedule, and buying a long-lived one stops being an option as maximum lifetimes fall to 47 days by 2029.
breaks.mitigation: Only the outside face is affected; the intranet runs on step-ca and does not notice. Renew through the offshore VPS over WireGuard when the direct path is filtered.

breaks.thing: Anything that was not mirrored before the cut
breaks.why: Mirrors are selective on purpose, so the first package, driver, docs set or 3D model that was not pulled is simply unavailable for the duration.
breaks.mitigation: Keep the pull-through caches warm so ordinary work stays covered, and treat each miss as a line item for the next mirror pass rather than an emergency.

breaks.thing: Cloud-tethered appliances already in the building
breaks.why: A printer or 3D printer that authenticates to a vendor stops when the vendor decides, which is not the same day the network does. By then the purchase decision is years old and irreversible.
breaks.mitigation: VLAN 40 with no WAN route, and refuse at purchase time anything that cannot live there. If it needs an account to function, it does not enter the building.

drills.name: 72-hour blackout drill
drills.pass: Every failure found becomes a ticket; the drill is over only when the list is empty
steps: Pull the cable at the router rather than writing a firewall rule; a rule you wrote is a rule you can have written wrong
Work a normal three days: documents, imaging, media, games, and an invoice issued on paper
Log every reach for a phone's LTE as a failure, including the small ones nobody would have mentioned
Check clocks at hour 72; without GPS this is the thing actually being tested
Convert each failure into a ticket before the cable goes back in, while the detail is still fresh

drills.name: Restore from cold media
drills.how: Restore a real dataset onto empty hardware using the cold HDD and the printed runbook only
drills.pass: An untested backup is a rumor. It passes when the data comes back and nobody had to open a laptop for instructions
steps: Pick a dataset that would actually hurt to lose, not the smallest one
Restore onto a wiped spare, never over the original
Time it, and record the number in the runbook so the next estimate is honest
Verify with restic check --read-data rather than trusting that the files listed

drills.name: DNS-is-dead card drill
drills.how: Point a workstation's resolver at nothing and reach three services using only the printed IP card
drills.pass: All three reached, with no certificate warning, which also proves the IP SANs were issued correctly
steps: Hand the card to someone who did not build the network and watch where they hesitate
Include one Yggdrasil address in the attempt, since that is the domain-seized path
Reprint the card if any address, fingerprint or SSID on it is stale

drills.name: Node A cold-loss failover
drills.how: Power node A down completely and bring the fleet up on node B at the second site
drills.pass: Serving again in under 24 hours, using the runbook and nothing that was stored only on node A
steps: Shut node A down cold rather than migrating gracefully
Promote the node B datasets and re-point DNS at the second site
Note every credential, script or note that turned out to live only on node A and move it

drills.name: Optical archive verify
drills.how: Read every archived disc back and check it against its own SHA256SUMS and PAR2 set
drills.pass: No unrecoverable errors; anything PAR2 had to repair gets reburned immediately rather than noted
steps: Verify on the spare burner as well as the primary, which also tests that the spare still works
Reconcile against the disc registry and chase any disc listed but not on the shelf
Reburn the crown-jewel set if the media is past ten years, regardless of whether it read cleanly

cadence.task: ArchiveBox crawl of the bookmark bar
Cold HDD swap, one copy always off-premises
Blackout drill, WAN unplugged for 72 hours
Disc integrity verify across the archive
Rebuild and re-sign the Fleet Offline Edition ISO
Reprint and redistribute the IP card
Archive vendor firmware and drivers for a new device
